title: Finite classical lisse Weil diagrams admit simultaneous normalized heart realizations
statement: Fix a prime power $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $Y_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and write $g_Y$ for geometric Frobenius. Use the classical lisse adic categories of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], the sf raw rationalized and common-stage constructible hearts of [def-weil-constructible-heart, def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients], and the normalized lisse realization of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization]. The scheme $Y$ is Noetherian of finite dimension and is a finite disjoint union of clopen connected components. Let $I$ and $A$ be finite sets of vertices and arrows, with source and target maps $A\rightrightarrows I$. At each vertex prescribe a classical lisse $\Omega$-sheaf $M_i$ with a Weil isomorphism $\theta_i:g_Y^*M_i\xrightarrow{\sim}M_i$, where $g_Y^*$ is the classical lisse pullback of [def-wf-lisse-adic-automorphism-pullback]; along each arrow prescribe a Weil-equivariant rational sheaf map. Prescribe finitely many equations between finite additive composites of these maps, their Frobenius pullbacks, the Weil maps and their inverses. Then there are a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in $\Omega$, classical lisse $E$-models for all these objects, arrows, inverse maps and equations, and normalized inverse systems $N_i=(N_{i,n})_{n\geq1}$ of finite locally free $\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$-sheaves with locally constant finite ranks, whose rationalizations are those models. Each $N_i$ gives a lisse sf heart object $K_i$ whose module realization is $\widehat N_i[1/\varpi_E]$, where $\widehat N_i=\varprojlim_n\nu_Y^*N_{i,n}$. The normalized Hom identifications lift all the prescribed maps, inverses and equations, and give Weil isomorphisms $Lg_Y^*K_i\xrightarrow{\sim}K_i$ and Weil-equivariant arrow maps. These identifications use the actual Frobenius pullbacks with the unit pinning of [def-zl-normalized-classical-weil-realization] and are compatible with finite coefficient extension. The rational maps need not preserve the chosen integral systems. After scalar extension to $\Omega$, any prescribed Weil-compatible identification of one $M_i$ with the realization of a given lisse heart Weil object (one carrying $\theta_i$ to the realized Weil structure of that object) lifts uniquely to a Weil isomorphism with that object. Zero objects, zero maps, an empty diagram, and disconnected or empty $Y$ are allowed.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1),(4) and Proposition 6.8.14(2); finite Hom-colimit diagrams and underlying stable lattices (Weil II (1.1.1)b-d; Stanford L19 Proposition 1.1.9). Agent refinement for blueprint real-mixed-by-curves paragraph 1.

proof.text: Choose coherent finite stages P0 for the supplied realization R using lem-zl-coherent-normalized-diagram-stages. Apply lem-zl-finite-weil-diagram-descent to the finite classical diagram and its equations, obtaining E,N,b,beta and the raw signed-expression equalities.

At the chosen stage, its finite_add field induces an additive homomorphism from the underlying raw Hom group to the sf Hom group. An additive homomorphism preserves integer scalar multiples and finite list sums; induction on the expression list therefore sends each raw expression value to the corresponding finite value. Apply this homomorphism to each descended equation. The stage lisse field supplies finite lissity.

The geometric fibre is noetherian by the inherited zlClassicalNoetherian instance. A locally noetherian scheme is locally connected; compactness then makes its connected-component quotient finite, and every connected component is clopen. A finite lisse object is common-stage lisse by reusing its local free charts and applying the finite-to-common pullback object equality. This property is invariant under isomorphism by composing each chart isomorphism with pullback of the inverse isomorphism. Apply it to stage inverse followed by R.functor.mapIso beta to obtain common-stage lissity of each supplied classical object.

For each classical vertex apply lem-zl-prescribed-weil-isomorphism-lifts. Assemble the descended diagram, its finite equations, component topology, finite and common lissity, coefficient coherence and unique prescribed-object lifts into the unchanged conclusion.

tool_uses.why: Use only its Noetherian, finite-dimensional, invertible-coefficient conclusion for finite-type geometric schemes; the unit contains no replacement for these scheme hypotheses.
Finite irreducible components are a generic Noetherian topological tool for choosing lattices componentwise.
Classical finite and adic fibre equivalences turn underlying sheaves into profinite representations and lattice reductions back into sheaves.
The compact-group stable-lattice theorem applies to geometric monodromy only, not to the Weil group.
Use reduction/limit equivalence and fully faithful rationalization with actual pullback and coefficient comparisons.
Use the actual inverse-limit integral complex and its raw sf heart realization, not a new definition of the heart.
Use the specified fully faithful sf lisse-heart realization, ordinary pullback, unit and finite-extension normalizations.
The identity-induced sf/PBC coefficient bridge gives the identical finite-reduction pullback tower required by the normalized model datum.
Canonical continuous integral reduction equivalence supplies the actual reduction datum and quotient maps for unit pinning.
Fix the coefficient isomorphism by its actual finite-quotient projections; this avoids silently choosing a scalar automorphism.
Existence of Comparison records with the prescribed integral datum and coefficient isomorphism, needed before applying the operation theorem.
Use the actual-adjunction-unit normalization of completed tensor pullback operations for the comparisons, not an unproved existence assertion from a definition.
